about: Held-out generalisation target G34, in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a real assembly: three printed bodies (drawer, housing, stop), two catalogue magnets placed from the parts catalogue, dovetail rails and grooves at a stated clearance, magnet pockets, and fit, travel and tolerance requirements judged by sweeping the bodies and measuring gaps on the delivered STLs. L1 ids match requirements.md next to this file, which holds the L2/L3 tree, the reference models, the assumptions and the traceability. Numbers that are not in the request words (rail angle band, pocket sizes, wall range, size limit) come from requirements.md and are provisional until the owner confirms them. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in generalize/parts/*/part.json.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the board in, load path, slide the drawer)

requests.title: Sliding drawer with dovetail rails and magnet detent
requests.request: A small parts drawer, 80 mm long, 60 mm wide and 25 mm tall counting its rails, that slides in a printed housing on two dovetail rails. Each rail has 0.3 mm of clearance per side in its groove. A 6 x 3 mm neodymium disc magnet sits in a pocket in the back of the drawer and another in the housing's back wall; with the drawer shut the two magnets are 0.5 mm apart and hold it closed. The drawer has to stop at 70 mm of travel so it cannot be pulled out by accident, but it must still come out for assembly. The drawer, the housing and the stop are separate printed parts that go together by hand with no screws, printed on an FDM printer without supports.
requests.request_verbatim: A small parts drawer 80 x 60 x 25 mm that slides in a housing on two dovetail rails with 0.3 mm clearance per side. A 6 x 3 mm neodymium magnet pocket in the drawer and another in the housing hold it closed with the magnets 0.5 mm apart. Stop the drawer at 70 mm travel.
requests.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, all from requirements.md section 3: 80 x 60 x 25 includes the rails (D2); magnets seated on the pocket floors and the 0.5 mm measured between their faces (D3, A4); stop is a separate removable part so the drawer can be assembled (D4, A5); no fasteners, FDM, no supports (A7).

l1.text: The drawer shall be an open-top tray whose overall size, rails included, is 80 mm long (sliding direction), 60 mm wide and 25 mm tall.

The drawer shall carry two dovetail rails, one on each side, each protruding 2 to 5 mm with flanks 48 to 65 degrees from the drawer's width axis, that run in two matching dovetail grooves in the housing, with 0.3 mm of clearance per side between each rail flank and its groove flank.

The drawer shall slide freely from closed to 70 mm of travel, touching nothing, with at least 0.3 mm to the housing everywhere (0.3 to 0.6 mm above and below the drawer when shut), and at 70 mm at least 8 mm of each rail shall still be in its groove.
With the stop in place the drawer shall be stopped at 70 mm of travel (69.5 to 70.5 mm) by a stop that is a separate part and that bears on the drawer over at least 6 mm2.

The drawer's back and the housing's back wall shall each have a pocket for one 6 x 3 mm disc magnet (0.1 to 0.3 mm wider and 0.15 to 0.35 mm deeper than the magnet, so that the seated magnet is recessed 0 to 0.6 mm below its wall face), the two pockets coaxial, so that with the drawer shut the two seated magnets are 0.5 mm apart (0.4 to 0.6 mm).
With the drawer shut it shall rest against the housing's back wall with its front face flush with the housing's front face, and the closed assembly shall have no interference.

The rails shall hold the drawer: at every position from closed to 70 mm it shall not be possible to lift it or move it sideways by 1 mm; the play shall be 0.3 to 0.45 mm sideways each way and 0.4 to 1.2 mm in total vertically, and at 70 mm travel the drawer shall tilt 1 to 8 degrees before touching the housing.
The drawer, the housing and the stop shall be three separate printed bodies that go together by hand with no fasteners; with the stop removed the drawer shall slide straight out of the housing.

All walls, floors and rails shall be strong enough to print and use: housing roof, floor and back wall 2.0 to 5.5 mm and side walls 2.0 to 7.0 mm, drawer walls 1.6 to 5.0 mm (back wall up to 6.0 mm), rail necks at least 3.0 mm, and the stop at least 6.0 mm2 in section.
Each of the three bodies shall be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports in its stated print orientation.
The housing shall be no larger than 90 x 70 x 35 mm, have a flat underside, and stand on a desk without tipping.

The design shall be delivered as a drawer STL, a housing STL, a stop STL (closed assembly pose, mm), the OpenSCAD source, a manifest declaring the magnet poses, the stop's removal direction and each body's print orientation, and the agent's own measurement report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.

beyond_library: dovetail profile (trapezoid extrusion) on a body and its offset negative in a second body at a stated normal clearance
sliding assembly: poses of the same body at different travel positions, sweeps and first-contact distance as checks
magnet pockets from a catalogue part (pocket diameter and depth derived from the magnet, recess so the faces are a stated gap apart)
three printable bodies, one of them a removable stop, each with its own print orientation
tolerance stack on a gap built from measured depths and catalogue tolerances
rotation clearance: tilt of the drawer at full extension from the engaged rail length and the clearances
